item.title: Blockchain Multi Discriminator Network Shields Social Internet of Things From Attacks - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Generative adversarial network and blockchain architecture for zero-day intrusion detection in social Internet of Things networks
  • Article Title: Blockchain-anchored multi-discriminator GAN architecture for real-time zero-day attack detection in social IoT edge networks with explainable audit trails
  • Blockchain-anchored multi-discriminator GAN architecture for real-time zero-day attack detection in social IoT edge networks with explainable audit trails. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 140. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00486-5

본문

A research team led by Sneha Kanawade, Nilkanth Deshpande, Shilpa Gite, and Nilima Dongre has developed an intrusion detection framework named BMG-Sentinel, designed to secure Social Internet of Things edge deployments against previously unencountered zero-day cyber threats while maintaining an immutable, regulator-ready forensic audit trail. Published in Discover Internet of Things, the investigation tackles the dual challenges of detecting sophisticated zero-day incursions in decentralized device ecosystems and establishing tamper-evident accountability for automated mitigation decisions. The investigators engineered a multi-discriminator generative adversarial network architecture integrated with a permissioned blockchain ledger, off-chain cryptographic storage, and a multi-method explainability pipeline. By distributing discrimination tasks across three specialized neural network modules that concurrently evaluate packet signatures, host behavioral sequences, and network graph topology, the system overcomes the structural blind spots of conventional single-discriminator generative models. Experimental evaluations conducted on heterogeneous benchmark corpora demonstrated that this architectural arrangement attained an overall F1-score of 0.942 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.974 when evaluated against held-out zero-day attack classes, surpassing six established machine learning baselines while preserving low-latency inference on edge-grade hardware platforms.

item.title: INVE 테크놀로지스, IoT 사업 매각 이익 산출 내역 공개…인수에 3000만 달러 배정 - 데이터투자
item.description:
요약

  • 3분기 분기보고서 제출…현금 2341만 달러 지급하고 트랙소노미 우선주 5000만 달러어치 받아
  • 보고서에 따르면 회사는 태국 자회사 아이덴티브 타일랜드(Identiv (Thailand) Co., Ltd) 지분을 포함한 IoT 사업 영업자산 대부분과 함께 조정 대상인 현금 2500만 달러를 트랙소노미 시스템즈(Trackonomy Systems, Inc.)에 넘겼다.
  • 그 대가로 트랙소노미의 시리즈 C 우선주 5000만 달러어치(주당 공정가치 20.07달러)를 받았고, 트랙소노미는 IoT 사업 관련 일부 부채를 인수했다.

본문

3분기 분기보고서 제출…현금 2341만 달러 지급하고 트랙소노미 우선주 5000만 달러어치 받아

보고서에 따르면 회사는 태국 자회사 아이덴티브 타일랜드(Identiv (Thailand) Co., Ltd) 지분을 포함한 IoT 사업 영업자산 대부분과 함께 조정 대상인 현금 2500만 달러를 트랙소노미 시스템즈(Trackonomy Systems, Inc.)에 넘겼다. 그 대가로 트랙소노미의 시리즈 C 우선주 5000만 달러어치(주당 공정가치 20.07달러)를 받았고, 트랙소노미는 IoT 사업 관련 일부 부채를 인수했다. 이 거래는 9월 10일 연례 주주총회에서 승인됐으며, 회사는 9월 30일 현재 이 우선주 249만 1281주를 보유하고 있다.

매각 이익 612만 7000달러는 매각 대가 5000만 달러에서 매각 관련 현금 지급액 2341만 1000달러, 매각한 순자산 1750만 8000달러, 순운전자본 등 사후 정산 조정액 246만 5000달러, 거래 관련 비용 48만 9000달러를 뺀 값이다. 매각 시점 IoT 사업의 자산은 2032만 달러, 부채는 281만 2000달러였다. 회사는 사후 정산 조정분 250만 달러를 미지급금으로 계상해 매각 이익에서 차감했고, 이 금액은 4분기에 지급했다.

트랙소노미 우선주는 공정가치를 쉽게 알 수 없는 비상장 지분이어서 원가에서 손상을 빼고 같은 발행사의 동일·유사 증권에서 관찰되는 가격 변동을 반영하는 측정 대안 방식으로 회계 처리한다. 회사는 보고 기간 중 손상 징후는 없었다고 밝혔다. 회사는 매각 종결과 함께 6~12개월 동안 트랙소노미에 정보기술(IT)·인력을 지원하는 전환 서비스 계약도 맺었으며, 3분기 이 계약에서 발생한 수수료는 미미했다.

에드워드 커른바우어(Edward Kirnbauer) 최고재무책임자(CFO) 등 일부 직원은 자산 매각과 관련한 거래 보너스를 받을 자격이 있다. 보너스는 매각 종결 후 6~12개월의 잔류 기간이 끝나는 시점과 회사 해산 시점 중 이른 때에 지급되며, 원칙적으로 그때까지 계속 근무해야 한다. 회사는 지난 9월 전임 최고경영자(CEO)가 사임하고 임시 CEO가 선임됐다며, 정식 CEO 등 경영진 확보가 향후 실적을 좌우할 것이라고 밝혔다.

인수 3000만 달러 배정과 운영비 계획

회사는 매각 이후 상업적 영업 매출이 없는 상태에서 규제 산업의 기업용 서비스형 소프트웨어(SaaS) 기업 인수를 추진하고 있다. 대상 시장으로는 의료 운영, 작업자 안전(EHS), 의약품 공급망, 식품 안전, 의료기기 규제 준수, 환경·수질 관리, 산업 운영을 꼽았다. 회사는 가능한 한 빨리 인수를 마무리할 계획이지만 예정대로 성사된다는 보장은 없다고 밝혔다.

회사는 인수에 약 3000만 달러를 배정하고, 2027년부터 약 3년에 걸쳐 본사 관리비와 상장사 운영 비용으로 약 1200만~1500만 달러를 쓸 것으로 예상했다. 인수 대금은 현금과 함께 기간 가득형 주식, 프리미엄 가격의 옵션·워런트, 성과 연동 언아웃 등을 섞어 마련할 방침이다. 향후 현금 유입은 트랙소노미 전환 서비스 대금(발생하는 경우)과 이자수익으로 이뤄질 것이라고 회사는 설명했다.

9월 30일 기준 운전자본은 8140만 달러로 지난해 말 1억 3330만 달러보다 5190만 달러 줄었다. 1~9월 영업활동 현금 유출은 1377만 6000달러로 전년 동기 972만 9000달러보다 늘었고, 투자활동 현금 유출은 매각 관련 현금 지급액을 포함해 2517만 5000달러였다. 9월 30일 기준 누적 결손금은 3억 6560만 달러이며, 회사는 보유 현금으로 향후 최소 12개월간 운영 자금을 충당할 수 있다고 판단했다.

회사는 자사주 매입 프로그램에 따라 1~9월 보통주 61만 1144주를 180만 달러에 사들였다. 월별로는 8월 52만 6014주(평균 2.88달러), 9월 8만 5130주(평균 2.81달러)다. 프로그램 시행 이후 누적 매입은 107만 4923주, 약 370만 달러다. 이와 별도로 RSU 가득에 따른 직원 원천징수 세금 납부를 위해 보통주 30만 8335주(92만 9000달러)를 매입했다. 회사는 분기 종료 후인 10월 21일 주당 2.85~3.40달러로 최대 2000만 달러 규모의 수정 더치 옥션 방식 자사주 공개매수에 착수했으며, 이 공개매수는 뉴욕 시간 기준 11월 19일 오후 5시에 마감된다.

회사는 위험 요인에서 IoT 사업 매각 이후 나스닥 상장 규정상 '공개 셸(public shell)' 회사로 간주될 수 있으며, 그 경우 상장폐지 절차나 더 엄격한 상장 요건이 적용될 수 있다고 밝혔다. 현재 나스닥 상장폐지 계획은 없다고 덧붙였다. 1940년 투자회사법(Investment Company Act)상 투자회사로 간주되면 사업 전략 실행이 어려워져 회사를 청산하거나 정리하기로 결정할 수도 있다고 적었다.

트랙소노미 우선주는 공개시장이 없고 양도 제한이 붙어 있어 원하는 시점이나 가격에 처분하지 못할 수 있다고 회사는 밝혔다. 비상장사인 트랙소노미의 재무·영업 정보는 회계 처리상 공시가 필요한 범위 외에는 정기적으로 제공할 계획이 없다고 덧붙였다.

INVE 테크놀로지스는 IoT 사업 매각 후 아이덴티브(Identiv)에서 사명을 바꾼 회사로, 규제 산업에서 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)를 접목할 기업용 SaaS 사업의 인수·운영을 추진하고 있다. 본사는 미국 캘리포니아주 산타애나에 있다.

item.title: Hybrid Algorithm Improves 6G Massive MIMO Spectral Efficiency in Simulated IoT Networks - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Optimization of joint hybrid beamforming and underlay spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks
  • Article Title: Adaptive DEBKA for joint beamforming and spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks
  • Adaptive DEBKA for joint beamforming and spectrum sharing in 6G massive MIMO IoT networks. Discover Internet of Things, 6(1), Article 166. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43926-026-00509-1

본문

In simulated wireless communications research, an optimization algorithm known as the Differential Evolution-Enhanced Adaptive Black-Winged Kite Algorithm demonstrated substantial performance improvements for joint hybrid beamforming and underlay spectrum sharing across dense sixth-generation Internet-of-Things networks. Conducted by researchers Wenjian Zhang and Ping Li and published in Discover Internet of Things, the numerical study evaluated how coordinated radio-frequency beamforming and dynamic frequency allocation can overcome severe physical-layer bottlenecks in massive multiple-input multiple-output base stations. Under a default simulated configuration comprising 128 transmit antennas, eight radio-frequency chains, 50 single-antenna devices, and 16 shared subchannels, the proposed algorithm attained an aggregate spectral efficiency of 15.87 ± 0.19 bits per second per Hertz over 30 independent Monte Carlo trials. This performance represents an advantage of 27.5 percent over the manifold-optimization alternating minimization baseline and 8.1 percent over the static hybrid BKAPI method. Furthermore, the search procedure achieved its one-percent convergence stopping threshold in an average of 185 ± 12 iterations, substantially reducing the iteration count required by standard metaheuristic benchmarks while enforcing strict hardware and interference boundaries.

The engineering challenge addressed by the study stems from the fundamental architecture of massive multiple-input multiple-output systems envisioned for upcoming 6G applications, including industrial automation, immersive communication, and intelligent transportation infrastructure. To mitigate these hardware burdens, network designers implement hybrid analog and digital beamforming, which cascades a low-dimensional digital baseband precoder with an analog phase-shifting network driven by a drastically smaller pool of radio-frequency chains. While hybrid architectures preserve much of the spatial multiplexing and array gain of fully digital setups, the physical phase shifters impose non-convex constant-modulus constraints where the magnitude of each analog precoding element must remain fixed to a constant unit value while only its phase angle is adjusted. Compounding this challenge, massive Internet-of-Things deployments require multiple devices to concurrently share identical subchannels, demanding meticulous multi-user interference management alongside strict interference-temperature constraints to protect primary licensed incumbents.

item.title: Smart Bin IoT Network Tests Waste Monitoring Across Bukavu Pilot Sites - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Subject of Research: Internet of Things network architecture for urban waste monitoring in Bukavu
  • Article Title: Design of an IoT sensor-based network architecture for waste collection in Bukavu city (DRC)
  • Design of an IoT sensor-based network architecture for waste collection in Bukavu city (DRC).

본문

A twelve-week pilot deployment of an Internet of Things network architecture in the eastern city of Bukavu in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has demonstrated the technical feasibility of real-time bin monitoring and algorithmic route optimization under challenging urban and topographical conditions. Researchers designed and evaluated a multi-tier framework that pairs downward-facing ultrasonic distance sensors installed in waste receptacles with low-power wide-area wireless transmissions and an open-source data analytics engine. In Bukavu, rapid urbanization, steep topography, and degraded secondary road infrastructure have combined to create severe municipal waste management deficits, where approximately 898 tons of solid waste are generated each day but formal municipal collection systems capture only about seven percent, or roughly 62.86 tons daily. Uncollected waste frequently accumulates across informal dumping sites located in drainage gutters, water collection areas, and public spaces, exacerbating environmental contamination and public health risks related to cholera and malaria transmission.

To evaluate whether low-power digital infrastructure could establish reliable monitoring in an environment marked by severe electrical and connectivity limitations, the investigation deployed seven smart waste bin prototypes across residential, dense, and peri-urban neighborhoods. The hardware architecture selected for the field test utilized Milesight EM310-UDL ultrasonic distance sensors, which were chosen following comparative assessments against alternative units such as the DF703 due to their operating range of up to 450 centimeters, wide angular accuracy of 60 degrees, and integrated accelerometer capabilities. The sensors operate on long-life batteries specified for up to ten years of service, an essential attribute given that only 17.8 percent of household energy needs in Bukavu are met by the electrical grid. To transmit data without incurring recurrent cellular subscription charges or exceeding local power constraints, the team configured the sensors to transmit over the LoRaWAN wireless protocol across the 863 to 870 megahertz frequency plan, routing packets through a centrally placed Things Indoor Gateway connected via an intermediate server on The Things Network.

item.title: The Path to Trillions Runs Through Networks - RFID Journal
item.description:
요약

  • Yet despite shipping billions of RFID tags and wireless trackers, the world is still operating in the dark 99.9% of the time. Most things that are made aren’t connected to the cloud in any way that is autonomous. Scans are snapshots, not connections.
  • So why is IoT the awkward stepchild of AI, when what we are really working on is a version of physical AI that could transform the economy?
  • We have all learned that the physical world is hard. I’d argue the reason is more specific than that: reading is still largely manual, and the readers that were supposed to be everywhere are not.

본문

Our industry has been working on something massively consequential for decades. Linking the physical world of places and things to the internet was always a huge idea. Add the power of AI applied to those things and the idea, and the opportunity, gets bigger still, especially if you believe that the full value of connecting physical things to the cloud has yet to be realized.

Yet despite shipping billions of RFID tags and wireless trackers, the world is still operating in the dark 99.9% of the time. Most things that are made aren’t connected to the cloud in any way that is autonomous. Scans are snapshots, not connections.

We will know we are succeeding when the links between digital and physical are counted in trillions, not billions, and, more importantly, when the cost of goods and the environmental impact of our supply chains are slashed. At that point we get to move beyond the basics of Maslow’s hierarchy to the joyful stuff: AI that goes beyond writing emails to giving us better tasting fruit, more effective medicines, and the kind of storytelling for everyday things that today we only get at a farmers’ market, a Louis Vuitton store or a top restaurant. Can we agree we are not there yet?

So why is IoT the awkward stepchild of AI, when what we are really working on is a version of physical AI that could transform the economy?

Billions, Finally

Let’s give credit where it’s due. The low-cost Bluetooth tag segment is at last experiencing the accelerated growth that has been a long time coming. Based on planned deployments from the likes of Walmart, Amazon, IFCO, the US Postal Service and McDonald’s, Bluetooth will cross the billion-tag boundary by the end of next year. Not bad for a technology originally designed to replace the wires between keyboards and PCs. Optimists like me expect annual production to eclipse the RFID industry’s 35 to 70 billion units a year before too long.

But before we pat ourselves on the back, this is a long way short of the addressable market that ABI Research and the Bluetooth SIG put at over a trillion units. The gap between a billion and a trillion is not a matter of cheaper tags. We have spent decades driving down cost, and it hasn’t happened yet. Something else is missing.

What Ambient Actually Means

“Ambient” in ambient IoT usually gets associated with harvesting energy from the light and radio waves around us. That matters, but the quality that makes ambient IoT transformative is ubiquity, and ubiquity is a function of three costs: tags, infrastructure and labor.

item.title: AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices - Industrial Cyber
item.description:
요약

  • AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices
  • Also, input validation flaws made up 16% of the findings, covering missing checks, bounds and null-termination problems. Control flow and logic bugs accounted for the smallest share at 8%, including infinite loops, null dereferences, PRNG issues and recursion.
  • By affected component, core IP, TCP, UDP, ICMP and Ethernet accounted for the largest share of newly identified vulnerabilities at 29%, followed by other components at 25% and HTTP and web servers at 15%.

본문

AI tears through legacy TCP/IP stacks, exposing vulnerabilities across critical infrastructure, OT and IoT devices

Forescout Research’s Vedere Labs found that artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted vulnerability analysis reduced the time needed to examine foundational networking software from approximately nine months to 90 hours, uncovering 99 vulnerabilities across 10 widely used TCP/IP stacks. Titled ‘Finding Critical Infrastructure Bugs with Off-the-Shelf AI,’ the research, which tested generally available AI models against open-source software and proprietary binaries, identified 66 previously unknown vulnerabilities, of which 52% were rated high or critical severity. The automated static analysis cost approximately $935, averaging $2.58 per finding, while the AI-assisted system also rediscovered 40% of previously known vulnerabilities, demonstrating ability to identify flaws in software that had already undergone extensive manual research.

The findings highlight how AI is lowering the time and cost barriers to vulnerability discovery for both security researchers and potential attackers, with implications for operational technology (OT), Internet of Things (IoT), medical devices and critical infrastructure environments. TCP/IP stacks are embedded in connected products across these sectors, meaning vulnerabilities in shared software components can affect hundreds of downstream products from multiple vendors.

Forescout noted that legacy and unsupported devices present particular challenges because they may remain operational for decades and can be difficult or impossible to patch. The company urged organizations to prioritize vulnerabilities based on reachability, exploitability and operational impact, reduce unnecessary device exposure, isolate systems that cannot be patched, accelerate patching where fixes are available, and strengthen security requirements in procurement.

“AI did not eliminate the need for expert vulnerability researchers, but it dramatically compressed the work,” Daniel dos Santos, vice president for research at Forescout, said in a Thursday media statement. “With access to an effective AI-assisted workflow, vulnerabilities in complex embedded software can be found much faster and at a fraction of the cost, by security researchers and attackers alike. Our research demonstrates that AI is changing the economics of vulnerability discovery and accelerating the pace at which security teams need to identify, prioritize, and mitigate cyber risk. This is especially impactful for critical infrastructure, where legacy and difficult-to-patch devices may remain in service for years.”

TCP/IP stacks are embedded in products used across OT, IoT, medical devices, network equipment and other cyber-physical systems. Because the same underlying software can be used across products from multiple manufacturers, a single vulnerability can create risk across the broader technology supply chain.

Top 6 AIoT Development Platform Suppliers in 2026 for Connected Device and Application Development

release outlines key evaluation considerations for AIoT platforms, including developer tools, API integration, device connectivity and application deployment.

CALIFORNIA, CALIFORNIA, UNITED STATES, November 13, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Top 6 AIoT Development Platform Suppliers in 2026 for Connected Device and Application Development

This release outlines key evaluation considerations for AIoT platforms, including developer tools, API integration, device connectivity and application deployment.

HANGZHOU, China, November 12, 2026 â A 2026 supplier review of AIoT development platforms has shortlisted six vendors that connected-device teams commonly assess when a product programme needs both device-side firmware enablement and cloud application deployment. The review covers Tuya Smart, the developer-facing platform brand of Hangzhou Tuya Information Technology Co., Ltd., alongside Alibaba Cloud IoT Platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS IoT), Microsoft Azure IoT, Cumulocity (Software AG) and PTC ThingWorx. It is an editorial assessment compiled from vendor documentation and public company disclosures, not an audited market-share ranking.

Two structural changes explain why platform choice now behaves like a procurement constraint rather than a tooling preference. Connected products increasingly carry AI functions at device or gateway level, which moves firmware, module selection and model deployment into the same scope as the cloud console. In parallel, buyers now ask about deployment flexibility, covering public cloud, private cloud, edge and hybrid, before they review feature lists.

Grand View Research estimated the global AI platform market at USD 14.21 billion in 2024. That figure covers development, infrastructure and enablement platforms generally and does not isolate AIoT, so it is useful as directional context rather than as a budget benchmark for a device programme.

How this shortlist was compiled

The assessment applies five criteria drawn from documentation that vendors publish themselves. Device-side enablement asks whether a platform reaches modules, microcontrollers, firmware and application panels, or stops at the cloud boundary. Developer tooling and API surface asks what SDKs, integrated development environments and low-code generation paths are documented. Connectivity and protocol coverage asks which radio and network families are supported. Deployment options asks whether public cloud, private cloud, edge, on-premises and hybrid modes are available. Application and AI development asks how model management, knowledge bases and workflow orchestration are handled.
